(1) turbidity currents can travel long distances without losing their identity; (2) lateral spreading on the flat basin floor is an important factor in turbidite distribution; (3) the upper flow regime is a common feature of all flows studied; and (4) the complete Bouma interval sequence is not a necessary attribute of all turbidites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
turbidite characteristics are strongly dependent on the source area and flow path of the turbidity current.
turbidite deposits are complex, and they vary greatly in character from one flow to the next.
turbidites are not homogeneous, but vary greatly from flow to flow, and even from place to place within a flow deposit.
